gridExercises.label: Survey cabin
gridExercises.clue: Find the red target inside one grid square. Name the line on its left, then the line below it.

gridExercises.label: Pine shelter
gridExercises.clue: The shelter sits west of the stream and north of the trail bend.

gridExercises.label: Footbridge
gridExercises.clue: Look where the trail crosses the blue watercourse.

gridExercises.label: Trig point
gridExercises.clue: The trig point is on the highest closed contour in the northwest.

terrainFeatures.name: Hill
terrainFeatures.read: Closed contours with elevation increasing inward.

terrainFeatures.name: Depression
terrainFeatures.read: Closed contours with hachures or other legend-defined depression marks.

terrainFeatures.name: Valley
terrainFeatures.read: Contour bends usually point uphill; water often occupies the low line.

terrainFeatures.name: Spur
terrainFeatures.read: A tongue of higher ground projecting from a ridge; contour bends point downhill.

terrainFeatures.name: Ridge
terrainFeatures.read: A long crest of high ground with slopes falling away on both sides.

terrainFeatures.name: Saddle
terrainFeatures.read: A low pass between two higher areas, shaped like a shallow hourglass.

routeSequence.use: A linear feature that keeps you organized while you move.
A feature you expect to confirm along the route.
An obvious, close feature from which the final approach begins.
A feature beyond the destination that tells you if you went too far.

fieldRoutine: Audit the sheet: date, scale, legend, grid or datum, contour interval, and declination information.
Orient the map using known ground features or the approved compass method for that map.
Locate yourself using two or more reliable features.
Plan a route with a handrail, checkpoints, an attack point, and a catching feature.
Estimate distance and time; identify decision points and a turnaround condition.
Move checkpoint to checkpoint and confirm position whenever the terrain changes.
If the map and ground stop agreeing, halt, observe, and re-establish position before continuing.

practiceLadder.task: Read a real map margin, identify ten symbols, and plot grid references indoors.
Walk a familiar, permitted loop with a companion and confirm obvious features.
Add bearings and pace checks under qualified instruction on a controlled route.

foundationChecks: I read eastings first and northings second.
I can explain what four-, six-, and eight-figure precision means.
I check scale and contour interval before measuring or judging terrain.
I can distinguish grid, true, and magnetic north.
I use the map's current declination information instead of a memorized number.
I can name the major terrain forms from contour patterns.
I can build a route around handrails, checkpoints, an attack point, and a catching feature.
I stop and re-establish position when the map and ground disagree.
